candidates.tagline: Rivian's third sticker recall: the adventure EV that keeps mis-labelling its own door jamb
candidates.story: On November 27, 2026, Rivian issued recall 26V761 — its third label-related recall in a short span — covering roughly 1,500 R1S, R1T, and newly launched R2 vehicles because tire placard stickers show the wrong tire specifications after the tires were swapped between build and delivery but the labels were never updated; the fix is mailing replacement stickers.
candidates.why_funny: A company selling $70,000+ adventure-ready electric trucks has now recalled vehicles three separate times because it can't get the information on its own door-jamb sticker right.
candidates.alt: Rivian R1T electric pickup truck with a distinctive blue and grey artistic wrap, plugged into an EV charger at a shopping mall parking lot in Torrance, California

candidates.tagline: Allstate 'You're in Good Hands' — except the app, website, and roadside help
candidates.story: On November 23, 2026, Allstate's entire digital stack — website, mobile app, and app-based roadside assistance — went dark for over four days through the Thanksgiving travel week, leaving customers unable to log in, file claims, pay bills, or call for roadside help; as of November 27 the company had not disclosed the cause, while its tagline has always been 'You're in Good Hands.'
candidates.why_funny: An insurance company whose entire brand promise is reliability and peace of mind quietly became completely unreachable during the highest-stakes travel week of the year — with no explanation.
candidates.alt: Person sitting on a sofa using a laptop showing the Allstate website with 'let's start an insurance quote' on screen, the same site that went dark for four days over Thanksgiving 2026
